$comment: Toolkit product repo: full harness adapter with strict primary-checkout edit/commit policies, plus the local Bugbot stop gate. A scaffolded workspace ships NO Cursor guard at all (AIO-864 removed the cross-repo one), so this file lives only here. Every command is a LOCATOR, not a call: it reads the hook payload from stdin ONCE, resolves the repo root the agent is actually touching from that payload (`git -C <payload .cwd> rev-parse --show-toplevel` — the same shape .codex/hooks.json uses), checks the marker THERE, and re-emits the captured payload into .harness/adapters/cursor/dispatch.sh. This replaces ${CURSOR_PROJECT_DIR}, which resolves to ONE root chosen when the WINDOW opened. In a multi-root window anchored on a repo that does not vendor .harness/ (aios-team-brain, aios-website, a scaffolded workspace) that root has no marker, so the guards did not fail closed — they never ran at all, silently, for the whole session. Cursor does send a real .cwd for beforeShellExecution and preToolUse, and cursor/normalize.sh already prefers it; only the dispatch decision ignored it. ${CURSOR_PROJECT_DIR} is kept as the SECOND candidate, never as a replacement: the events that carry no per-repo location (stop, sessionStart) are session-scoped and have no better answer, and afterFileEdit is located by its own file_path. The payload cwd is read with jq, so a string that merely LOOKS like a cwd field — a file body being written, a shell command being run — is never mistaken for the real one. The sed fallback exists only so the dispatch decision does not REQUIRE jq, and it cannot be used to slip past a guard: with jq absent, cursor/dispatch.sh degrades every hook to a loud allow (or, under HARNESS_REQUIRE_JQ=1, to a block) before the resolved root can influence anything, so the fallback only ever picks which root receives a decision that is already fixed. The decision still keys on a MARKER FILE that identifies THIS repo specifically: scripts/toolkit-manifest.mjs, the toolkit's own manifest of what a workspace vendors. It is never itself vendored (absent from MANAGED_PATHS and from scaffold-project.sh, so no workspace and no unrelated root has it) and it cannot be absent from a valid toolkit checkout, because update.mjs and the manifest-parity test both import it. Marker ABSENT means the hook does not apply to that root (exit 0); marker PRESENT but the dispatcher missing means the toolkit's own guard is broken or deleted, which is exit 3 (could-not-evaluate, mapped to a block) so enforcement is never silently lost. The marker is deliberately NOT a generic path like .cursor/hooks or .harness — a scaffolded workspace legitimately has those and would be policed with the toolkit's strict policy — and deliberately NOT a file this repo may legitimately delete: the previous marker (scaffold/.cursor/hooks.json) was removed by AIO-864 itself, which silently downgraded the anti-tamper branch from exit 3 to exit 0. Only the LOCATOR is inline, because it is the one piece that has to run before any resolvable path exists; the superseded claim that the whole check had to be inline 'because a helper script would sit at the same unresolvable path' no longer holds, since the helper is reached through the payload-derived root. The locator text is byte-identical in every entry below (pinned by test/cursor-payload-dispatch.test.mjs), and each entry differs only in its trailing dispatcher arguments.

sessionStart.command: /bin/sh -c 'P=$(cat); M=$1; D=$2; shift 2; R=; X=$(printf '\''%s'\'' "$P" | jq -r '\''.cwd // .file_path // empty'\'' 2>/dev/null) || X=$(printf '\''%s'\'' "$P" | sed -nE '\''s/.*"(cwd|file_path)"[[:space:]]*:[[:space:]]*"([^"]*)".*/\2/p'\'' | tail -1); for C in "$X" "${CURSOR_PROJECT_DIR:-$PWD}"; do [ -n "$C" ] || continue; [ -d "$C" ] || C=$(dirname -- "$C"); T=$(git -C "$C" rev-parse --show-toplevel 2>/dev/null) || continue; [ -e "$T/$M" ] || continue; R=$T; break; done; [ -n "$R" ] || exit 0; [ -f "$R/$D" ] || { echo "AIOS hook: $R has the harness marker but $D is missing - refusing to run unguarded" >&2; exit 3; }; printf '\''%s'\'' "$P" | /bin/sh "$R/$D" "$R" "$@"' aios-cursor-hook scripts/toolkit-manifest.mjs .harness/adapters/cursor/dispatch.sh hook session_start inject-context.sh
